recipes.name: Vegetarian Moroccan Stew
ingredients_raw: 1 pound butternut squash - peeled, seeded, and cut into 2-inch cubes
4 large red potatoes, cut into 2-inch cubes
1 (14.5 ounce) can canned diced tomatoes with their juice

steps.text: Heat olive oil in a large covered saucepan or Dutch oven over medium heat, until oil is hot but not smoking. Drop in the onion, garlic, cumin, cinnamon stick, and salt and pepper. Cook and stir for 5 minutes, until onion is tender and translucent.

Stir in the butternut squash and potato cubes, broth, garbanzo beans, and tomatoes, and bring the mixture to a boil. Reduce heat, cover the pot, and simmer about 20 minutes, stirring occasionally, until the squash and potatoes are tender. Remove the stew from heat, and stir in the olives and lemon zest.

In a large saucepan, bring 1 3/4 cup water to a boil. Stir in couscous. Cover and remove from the heat; let stand for 5 minutes. Fluff with a fork; cool. Serve stew over cooked couscous. Garnish each serving with a dollop of yogurt and a sprinkle of cilantro leaves.

raw_recipe.headline: Vegetarian Moroccan Stew
raw_recipe.description: Butternut squash, potatoes, and chickpeas get a North African treatment in a stew flavored with cinnamon, tomatoes, and olives.

review.reviewBody: The first thing my husband noticed when he walked in the house was that it smelled just like the restaurants around the spice markets of Morocco! Though, he said, and I agree, that it was even fresher and better than any Moroccan dish, add some mint green tea and the traditional dessert of sliced oranges sprinkled with cinnamon and sugar and this may be your new favorite dish!

Stew was hearty and savory just like stew should be. You can easily adjust the recipe or make leftovers last longer by adding pine nuts, golden raisins, etc. My couscous was bland and stuck together. So, when making more for leftover stew, I sauteed minced garlic in 3 tbsp. olive oil, then added the water, brought to a boil, and added couscous. The couscous had garlic-olive oil flavor, and had much better texture than the first batch.

A good hearty vegetarian recipe. I had some cubed butternut waiting to be used, plus two chayote squash. I doubled the recipe, and between the two squashes, had nearly 2 lbs. I did not double the onion or garlic. Definitely recommend using golden raisins with the olives, rather than doubling the olives. Like others, I omitted the potatoes and used ground cinnamon. Mint was a good suggestion; we had both mint and cilantro. One thing that I think helped give it a better texture: use an inversion blender if you have one, before adding the olives and raisins. Whir it a bit until the color is a bit more opaque and creamy. We found the spice levels a bit mild, so added our favorite hot sauce.

Good base to adjust as you like for seasoning and what you have on hand. I followed it pretty closely, and like others, I had to double the cumin and used ground cinnamon in higher dose than the cinnamon stick (2 tsp?). In the end, I added ketchup to thicken it up a little, used about 1/2 tsp of dried orange rind I had, threw in about 1/4 cup raisins, two dashes of lemon juice and a dash each of cayenne, coriander, all spice, and ginger. After that, it was much more flavorful.

Great starting recipe. I added a carrot, few sprigs of thyme, 2 bay leaves a cup more vegetable stock and a teaspoon or so of tumeric. I omitted the topping. I prefer this as a soup rarther on top of the cous cous mainly because when i put it on the couscous it lost its flavour because the veggies didnt have the chance to absorb all the flavour in the short cooking time, but as a soup / stew alone it is yummy! It is one of those recipes I will make again because I always have those ingredients on hand.
This is always a favourite in our household. I add 2 carrots, chopped small red bell pepper, extra cup of broth and a little extra cumin. Turns out great everytime!
Will make again. I served with sourcream and harissa mixed and topped with a mixture of chopped cilantro and fresh mint. Served on Lebanese couscous (Moghrabieh). Super tasty!

i made this for my husband and he really liked it. he is not a big fan of exotic foods. however this went over well. changes: i used regular potatos rather than red potatos. i added one extra cup of vegetable broth in addition to the 2cups. i used the cinnamin stick but also added 1/2 TBSP of cinnamin. i also added one extra TBSP of ground cumin. i used 1TBSP of pepper and 1/2 TBSP of salt. i used only 1/2 the ammount of olives because my husband doesnt care for them. but i think he actually liked them in this dish. i bought plain, pitted olives in water and sea salt, so they were mild in flavor. i also added a bit of the olive juice to the stew just for added flavor. i still feel like it could have used something more, but overall it was a great new recipe to try and i will make it again!

My husband and I really enjoyed this dish; it was flavorful and satisfying. I did take some of the advice of other reviewers and added a can of tomato paste and 1 tsp. of ground cinnamon instead of using a cinnamon stick. I did cut the potatoes and squash in 2 inch pieces. As a result, the cooking time was much longer than specified. When I make this again, I will cut them in bite-sized pieces and alter the cooking time proportionately. For the couscous I sauteed garlic in a tsp. of olive oil then added the water and couscous. Overall, a great recipe.

I did not want to have a lot of clean up this evening so I made this in the crockpot and it was very good. I did add a 1/2 tsp of cinnamon in addition to the stick and 3tsp of cumin instead of 2 and a bit more water(as previous reviews suggested). I did not have potatoes so I did not use any and used 2 cans of chick peas to make it meatier. Delish. Will make again.
The house smells delicious! I didnt have canned tomatoes, so i used two cans of tomato paste. Turns out the stew was rich and thick!!!! Loved it on a bed of couscous or quinoa.
I didn't use the olives or cinnamon, and substituted turmeric for cumin. I had precooked the squash and dry garbanzo beans, so I added them near the end. Love the flavour!!
I made this without the olives and it was still delicious. Great recipee!
Amazing! I made it exactly as directed! It was delicious!
Delicious change from regular stew recipes!
This was an easy dish, only time consuming thing was dicing everything, but it cooked up fast. I used quinoa instead of couscous which increased protein in meal. Family loved it!!!
Awesome recipe! Thank you! I used sweet potatoes instead of squash and it turned out fabulous!
Husband and I thought it was delicious and had unique favors, different from the usual. Filling meal, too. Would make it again. Wonder if it would freeze well?

I liked this but didn't love it and I'm not sure why. Reading the recipe sounded like something I would really love but for some reason I felt it was off. Not sure why. I have to say that I love olives but they didn't taste good in this recipe. Not a big deal because you can just push them aside. This did taste better the next day so maybe the flavor just needed to mesh longer. Not sure if I'll make it again.
This was delicious!!! It made a lot of left overs as well.
